narrativeReportMd:
# PaymentReconciliation R4→R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
Breaking local changes were found. The same canonical resource exists in R6, but important wire names and content model shifted: R6 adds required root `type`, renames required `paymentDate` to `date`, renames required `paymentAmount` to optional `amount`, and replaces `detail` with `allocation`.

## Scope
This report covers local PaymentReconciliation definitions only. Base Resource/DomainResource/Element/Extension changes and search parameters are out of scope.

## Main migration themes
R4→R6 migration requires a structural transform, not only code-system updates. Existing instances need field renames, an explicitly derived root payment category, and allocation-reference review. R6→R4 conversion is lossy for optional R6-only payment instrument/source fields and for R6 instances that omit `amount`.

## Highest-impact findings
The hard breaks are mandatory root `type`, `paymentDate`→`date`, `paymentAmount`→`amount`, and `detail`→`allocation`. The main potential hard break after transformation is the narrower allocation reference model.

## Findings requiring human review
Manual policy is needed when deriving root `type`, handling R6 instances without `amount`, mapping broad R4 detail references, and preserving R6-only payment instrument/source data.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Several changes could have been introduced with aliases, optional transition fields, profiles, or extensions. R6 appears to prefer a clearer and richer payment allocation model over R4 wire compatibility.

## Follow-up analysis
Official ConceptMaps, narrative pages, and terminology expansions would improve confidence in semantic mappings.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `PaymentReconciliation` has material local R4→R6 breaks: mandatory root `type`, required field renames, and `detail`→`allocation`. R6 also introduces round-trip risks through optional amount and new payment metadata. The main uncertainty is the lack of official ConceptMaps for the redesign.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Implement migration as a structural transform: rename root payment fields, synthesize root `type`, rename `detail[]` to `allocation[]`, and review references whose target domain changed. For R6→R4, define extension/loss policies for R6-only content and reject or review instances missing `amount`.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural deltas because both StructureDefinitions were directly compared. Confidence is medium for semantic intent and terminology edge cases because official diffs, narrative pages, ConceptMaps, and full terminology expansions were not available.

findings.title: R6 adds mandatory root PaymentReconciliation.type

oldState.summary: R4 had no root `type`; payment category was required only on each `detail.type`.

semanticText.definition: Code to indicate the nature of the payment.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 instances could not carry a root payment category. If details existed, each detail required its own category.

newState.summary: R6 requires root `PaymentReconciliation.type` and makes `allocation.type` optional.

semanticText.definition: Code to indicate the nature of the payment such as payment, adjustment.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 requires one overall payment category at the resource root.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Name, short text, and payment-type binding connect R6 root `type` to R4 detail category, but the granularity changed from per-detail to root-level.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R6 validators require a root `type` that R4 instances do not have. R6→R4 also lacks a native root-category field; copying it into detail rows can be lossy or impossible when no detail exists.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent an overall category for the payment.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Add root `type` as optional and retain required allocation/detail type during transition, or require root `type` only in profiles.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Representing an overall payment category is a reasonable R6 goal, but the local evidence does not show why every base instance had to supply a new mandatory root element. A less-breaking design could preserve most R4 data, yet it would not give all base R6 resources the same normalized category guarantee and would need conflict rules when line-level and root-level categories differ.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The strongest less-breaking base design would introduce `PaymentReconciliation.type` as `0..1`, keep the old per-line category path required or otherwise valid, and use profiles or best-practice guidance where a single root category is required. That is only a partial alternative because no-detail and mixed-detail R4 instances still need policy decisions, and allowing both root and line categories can leave two same-resource representations for related payment-classification facts indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old instances but weakens the base guarantee of a single payment category and risks duplicate root-vs-line type representations.

evidence.detail: R4 detail.type is 1..1 CodeableConcept with example payment-type binding.
R6 root type is 1..1 CodeableConcept with extensible payment-type binding.

examples.examplesMd: Example is illustrative; full migration also handles other renamed required fields.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 requires a new root category. A migration cannot always infer one safely from R4 because R4 category was per-detail and absent when no detail rows existed.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old R4 JSON is R6-invalid until a root `type` is supplied. Generated R6 constructors and validators may reject missing type. R6 root type has no clean R4 field.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Derive `type` from business rules or a single consistent R4 `detail.type`; flag no-detail or mixed-detail-category instances for manual review. Test single, absent, and mixed category cases.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Keeping root `type` optional or retaining per-detail required type would have avoided the base validation break. The R6 choice improves consistency but forces a semantic migration decision.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: No official ConceptMap was available for root type derivation.

findings.title: Required paymentDate was renamed to required date

semanticText.definition: The date of payment as indicated on the financial instrument.

oldState.narrativeMd: Mandatory date of payment was serialized as `paymentDate`.

newState.summary: R6 requires the same concept at `date`.

semanticText.definition: The date of payment as indicated on the financial instrument.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 keeps type/cardinality/definition and changes the wire name to `date`.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Short, definition, type, cardinality, and summary flag match.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 `paymentDate` is unknown in R6 and R6 still requires `date`, so raw instances fail until renamed. Reverse mapping is straightforward.

justification.inferredGoal: Use a shorter/common root date name.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the R4 wire name `paymentDate` with the same date semantics and clarify the definition if needed.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal is a cleaner or more general root date name, but the type, cardinality, summary flag, and definition are otherwise the same. Retaining the R4 name would have preserved essentially all R4-valid instances while still communicating the payment-issued date, so the direct path break appears probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A backwards-compatible base R6 design could simply leave the element as `PaymentReconciliation.paymentDate` and update wording or aliases to explain that it is the payment date. Supporting both `paymentDate` and `date` as same-resource fields would also preserve data, but keeping the old name alone has lower duplication risk and only carries forward a nonoptimal legacy name.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old instances with only a modest naming cost; `date` is shorter but not semantically necessary.

findings.narrativeMd: This is a simple but hard wire-name break: the date value survives but the JSON property changes.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances with `paymentDate` are invalid against R6 because `date` is missing. R6 `date` can be renamed back for R4.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Rename `paymentDate` to `date` in R4→R6 and reverse it in R6→R4. Test required-date validation.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: An alias/deprecation period could have avoided the validation break; the tradeoff would be duplicate names for the same concept.

findings.title: Required paymentAmount was renamed to optional amount

semanticText.definition: Total payment amount as indicated on the financial instrument.

newState.summary: R6 uses `amount`, but base cardinality is optional.

semanticText.definition: Total payment amount as indicated on the financial instrument.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 keeps the same concept and type under a shorter name, and relaxes requiredness.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Short, definition, requirements, type, and summary flag match; path and min cardinality changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 data must rename `paymentAmount` to `amount` for R6. Valid R6 data may omit `amount`, which cannot satisfy R4 required `paymentAmount` without inventing a value.

justification.inferredGoal: Rename the amount field and allow broader payment contexts where amount may be absent.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the R4 `paymentAmount` element and, if R6 needs absent amounts, relax that same element to `0..1`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Allowing payment reconciliations without a known amount may be a reasonable R6 goal, but renaming the element was not necessary to accomplish it. Keeping `paymentAmount` and relaxing cardinality would preserve R4 instances and support the substantive R6 cardinality change with low long-term cost.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would keep `PaymentReconciliation.paymentAmount` as the total payment amount and change its base cardinality from `1..1` to `0..1` if optionality is desired. That would not solve R6-to-R4 export of omitted amounts, but that reverse-direction gap is inherent in relaxing cardinality and does not justify rejecting existing R4 wire names.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Keeps a longer legacy name but avoids the R4-to-R6 path break while still allowing R6 instances without an amount.

examples.examplesMd: R6 fragment omits amount, which is allowed in R6 but not valid in base R4.

findings.narrativeMd: The total amount has a name break and a reverse-version cardinality gap. Dropping or guessing this value can affect financial reconciliation.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4→R6 fails unless renamed. R6→R4 fails when `amount` is absent because R4 requires `paymentAmount`.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Rename when present. For R6→R4, reject or manually review resources without `amount`; do not default to zero unless business policy proves it.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Retaining the R4 name or keeping amount required would be more compatible. The R6 choice supports broader workflows but creates lossy reverse conversion.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Human review is needed for R6 instances without amount.

findings.title: The detail backbone was renamed and expanded as allocation

oldState.summary: R4 used repeating `detail` backbone entries for settlement particulars.

semanticText.definition: Distribution of the payment amount for a previously acknowledged payable.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 serialized line-level settlement allocation under `detail[]`.

newState.summary: R6 uses repeating `allocation` backbone entries and adds allocation-specific fields.

semanticText.definition: Distribution of the payment amount for a previously acknowledged payable.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 keeps the settlement concept but serializes it under `allocation[]`, with new child fields such as target, targetItem[x], account, encounter, and noteNumber.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Backbone cardinality, short, definition, and many child definitions match, so `detail`→`allocation` is a high-confidence rename/rework.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances with `detail` contain a property R6 no longer defines. R6 allocation-only children have no base R4 representation, so reverse conversion may require extensions or lose data.

justification.inferredGoal: Use allocation terminology and support richer payment allocation targeting.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the R4 `detail` backbone and add the richer R6 allocation children under that existing path.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Using allocation terminology and adding richer allocation details are reasonable R6 goals, but the old `detail` backbone already represented settlement distribution and could have hosted the new children. The break from `detail[]` to `allocation[]` therefore appears more like avoidable model cleanup than a necessary base incompatibility.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base R6 design could retain `PaymentReconciliation.detail` with clarified text such as settlement allocation details, then add `target`, `targetItem[x]`, `encounter`, `account`, and `noteNumber` under that same backbone. This avoids duplicate backbones and preserves FHIRPath/codegen paths. The tradeoff is carrying a less expressive legacy name, which is modest compared with invalidating every R4 instance that contains `detail`.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 paths and instances with low to moderate cost, but keeps a less precise legacy backbone name.

evidence.detail: R6 defines `allocation` 0..* BackboneElement with the same short/definition.
R6 adds allocation target, targetItem[x], encounter, account, and noteNumber.

examples.examplesMd: Backbone rename example; a full transform also handles root `type`, `date`, and `amount`.

findings.narrativeMd: `detail[]` became `allocation[]`. This breaks raw JSON, generated model properties, FHIRPath expressions, and profile paths. Some child fields map directly, but several new R6 children and the changed type/reference model need special handling.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 data with `detail` is invalid in R6 because the element is removed. R6 allocation fields such as `targetItem[x]`, `account`, `encounter`, and `noteNumber` cannot be represented natively in R4.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Rename `detail[]` to `allocation[]`, map same-definition children, and treat `type`, `request`, and `response` using separate rules. Update FHIRPath/search/profile references.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A transitional alias would have preserved R4 instances but introduced duplicate representations. R6 favors model cleanup over wire compatibility.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Inherited BackboneElement differences are not included.

findings.title: Allocation request/response references changed from broad Resource targets to narrower payment targets

oldState.summary: R4 `detail.request` and `detail.response` were broad Reference(Resource) links.

semanticText.short: Request giving rise to the payment
semanticText.definition: A resource, such as a Claim, the evaluation of which could lead to payment.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 allowed any resource target for detail request/response links.

newState.summary: R6 `allocation.target` is limited to Claim, Account, Invoice, Encounter, or Contract; `allocation.response` is limited to ClaimResponse.

semanticText.definition: Specific resource to which the payment/adjustment/advance applies.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 narrows the linkage model and changes request semantics to a payment subject.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: This is not a pure rename: R4 request meant the originating request, while R6 target means the subject being paid. Both are local allocation linkage fields and require migration review.

impact.impactRationaleMd: After renaming detail to allocation, some R4 broad references cannot fit the narrower R6 target sets. R6 targetItem/account/encounter details also lack R4 fields.

justification.inferredGoal: Make allocation links specific to payable subjects and ClaimResponse commitments.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep broad `Reference(Resource)` links as deprecated compatibility fields or express the narrowed targets as warnings/preferred profiles.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of distinguishing payable subjects and ClaimResponse commitments is reasonable and materially improves computability. A less-breaking base design exists, but keeping unconstrained `Reference(Resource)` in the base would continue accepting references that R6 is trying to classify more precisely, while preserving both old request/response and new target/response fields would require conflict and precedence rules.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best alternative is not conversion tooling but an R6 base shape that either leaves the old broad references valid with preferred-profile guidance, or keeps deprecated request/response compatibility fields beside the new allocation target model. This is only partial because broad references undermine uniform validation of payment targets, and duplicate linkage fields could diverge or persist indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves broad R4 references but materially weakens computable payment-subject semantics or creates duplicate old/new linkage paths.

evidence.detail: R6 allocation.target is limited to Claim, Account, Invoice, Encounter, Contract.
R6 allocation.response is limited to ClaimResponse.

examples.examplesMd: The R4 references use resource types allowed by R4 but outside the R6 target sets.

findings.narrativeMd: The linkage model changed from broad request/response references to a narrower payment-subject model. This can improve semantics but can invalidate or strand R4 references.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 references to resources outside the R6 allowed sets become invalid after migration. R6 target sub-elements cannot round-trip to R4 without extensions or loss.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inspect each old detail request/response target resource type. Map only allowed targets automatically; route others to extensions or manual review. Test out-of-set references.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The target narrowing could have been expressed as profile guidance rather than base restriction. That would preserve old data but reduce R6 conformance clarity.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The request-to-target mapping is semantic and should be reviewed against local financial workflows.

findings.title: Outcome required binding changed from remittance-outcome to payment-outcome

oldState.summary: R4 outcome had required binding to remittance-outcome.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: Local CodeSystem included queued, complete, error, partial.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 used the remittance-outcome terminology canonical.

newState.summary: R6 outcome has required binding to payment-outcome.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: Local R6 payment-outcome CodeSystem includes the same four lexical codes.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 uses a new payment-outcome canonical with the same inspected code values.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Same element path/type/cardinality; local code lists match, but canonical changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Primitive code values appear unchanged, so JSON validation is unlikely to break for known codes. Codegen enum names, terminology canonical checks, and system-specific logic may still break.

justification.inferredGoal: Rename outcome terminology from remittance to payment.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: inspected primitive outcome codes appear unchanged, so this is not an R4-to-R6 base instance-compatibility break.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Renaming the outcome terminology from remittance to payment is a plausible cleanup, and the local code sets inspected for the required binding use the same four lexical codes. Existing R4 instance values should therefore remain acceptable in R6; the remaining risk is for generated terminology metadata, cached canonicals, and systems that key logic on the old value-set identity.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Under the calibration rules, no backward-compatible base-design alternative is applicable for preserving R4 instances because the JSON code values appear preserved. Keeping the old canonical as an alias or publishing an explicit ConceptMap would be useful for terminology tooling, but that is not the same as a less-breaking base R6 resource design.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Terminology aliases or ConceptMaps can reduce runtime/canonical churn, but they are governance and migration mitigations rather than a less-breaking instance-shape design.

evidence.detail: Inspected bound CodeSystems both contain queued, complete, error, partial.

examples.examplesMd: `"outcome":"queued"` appears lexically valid in both inspected bindings; risk is mainly terminology canonical/enum churn.

findings.narrativeMd: The required binding changed canonical, but the primitive code values inspected locally are the same. Treat this as a runtime/codegen and terminology-governance risk rather than a clear instance break.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Known R4 outcome codes should still validate lexically in R6. Systems tied to the old ValueSet/CodeSystem canonical or generated enum class may need updates.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Regenerate terminology bindings and verify all four outcome codes. Use an approved ConceptMap or local policy before treating remittance-outcome and payment-outcome as equivalent.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A retained alias or formal ConceptMap would reduce disruption. The rename is probably a terminology cleanup but still affects code-system integrations.

findings.title: paymentIssuer can now reference Patient or RelatedPerson in addition to Organization

semanticText.definition: The party who generated the payment.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 treated the payment issuer as an Organization reference.

newState.summary: R6 paymentIssuer may reference Organization, Patient, or RelatedPerson.

semanticText.definition: The party who generated the payment.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 supports patient-pay and related-person payment sources directly.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Same path, cardinality, and definition; only target profiles were added.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 Organization references remain valid in R6, but R6 Patient/RelatedPerson issuers cannot validate in base R4 without remapping or extensions.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: R6 widens `paymentIssuer` targets while preserving the R4 Organization target.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Allowing patient or related-person payment issuers is a reasonable R6 goal, and the widened target set keeps the R4 Organization target valid. Existing R4 instances are preserved in the R4-to-R6 direction, so the compatibility issue is limited to reverse conversion and organization-only implementation assumptions.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No less-breaking base R6 alternative is needed for old-instance preservation because the base design is already additive for R4 data. Extensions, rejection policies, or profiles may be needed when exporting R6 Patient/RelatedPerson issuers to R4, but those are down-conversion mitigations rather than backwards-compatible base-design alternatives.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: No R4-to-R6 base-design break; R6-to-R4 exchange must constrain or map newly allowed Patient and RelatedPerson issuers.

evidence.detail: R6 targets are Organization, Patient, RelatedPerson.

examples.examplesMd: Patient issuer is valid in R6 but not under the R4 target profile.

findings.narrativeMd: This is a safe widening for R4→R6 but a reverse-conversion and runtime-assumption risk for systems that modeled issuer as Organization-only.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old Organization references remain valid. New Patient/RelatedPerson references are R6-valid but not base-R4-valid in this field.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update generated types and validators. For R6→R4, reject, extend, or policy-map non-Organization issuers.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A separate optional field would preserve old type assumptions but fragment the issuer concept. The R6 widening is simpler for new workflows.

findings.title: processNote.text changed from string to markdown

oldState.summary: R4 process note text was primitive `string`.

semanticText.definition: The explanation or description associated with the processing.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 represented the text as plain string.

newState.summary: R6 process note text is primitive `markdown`.

semanticText.definition: The explanation or description associated with the processing.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 keeps the same path but gives the text markdown semantics.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Both primitives serialize as JSON strings, and inspected markdown derives from string. Ordinary values should remain wire-valid, but generated types and rendering/sanitization behavior can change.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `processNote.text` as `string` and allow markdown by convention, or add a separate optional markdown note field.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Formatted process-note text is a reasonable goal, and the change does not appear to be a normal JSON wire-shape break because markdown still serializes as a string. Less-breaking designs exist for generated APIs and strict type models, but they either fail to signal markdown semantics computably or split one note text across duplicate fields.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could retain `PaymentReconciliation.processNote.text` as `string` with documentation that markdown may be used. That preserves R4 codegen assumptions but leaves consumers unable to infer from the type that markdown rendering and sanitization rules apply. Adding a sibling markdown field would make the signal computable but creates duplicate same-resource representations for the same explanatory note.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Convention-only markdown weakens computable rendering semantics; a second field duplicates the same note text and risks divergence.

evidence.detail: Inspected markdown primitive derives from string with no narrower local regex.

examples.examplesMd: The JSON string can be carried to R4, but R4 consumers may display markdown markers literally.

findings.narrativeMd: `processNote.text` now advertises markdown semantics. This mainly affects codegen, rendering, and sanitization rather than validation of ordinary JSON strings.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Not a typical old-valid/new-invalid break because wire shape is still a JSON string. Runtime handling may differ if markdown is rendered.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Regenerate models and decide how to render or escape markdown-sensitive text. Test characters such as `*`, `_`, links, and line breaks.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Using markdown is computably clearer; keeping string would have avoided type churn but hidden formatting intent.

findings.title: R6 adds optional payment-source, instrument, note, and allocation fields with no native R4 representation

affectedLocation.newPath: PaymentReconciliation.statusReason; kind; enterer; issuerType; location; method; cardBrand; accountNumber; expirationDate; processor; referenceNumber; authorization; tenderedAmount; returnedAmount; processNote.class; processNote.number

oldState.summary: R4 had no native fields for these payment-source, payment-instrument, and process-note metadata elements.
oldState.narrativeMd: Same-path elements are absent from R4 PaymentReconciliation.

newState.summary: R6 adds optional fields for status reason, payment kind/source, collection/instrument details, tendered/returned amounts, and process-note metadata.
newState.narrativeMd: The fields are optional in R6, so they do not break R4→R6 validation, but they create R6-only content.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: These paths appear in the R6 differential and not in the R4 PaymentReconciliation element set.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Optional additions are not R4→R6 breaks. They are representability risks because base R4 has no native slots; dropping fields can lose audit and payment details.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent richer payment source/instrument/audit data directly.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: these are optional R6 additions and do not invalidate R4 PaymentReconciliation instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding optional payment-source, instrument, authorization, tendered/returned amount, process-note, and allocation metadata is a compatibility-friendly way to increase R6 expressiveness. The report correctly identifies reverse-conversion risk, but that is not evidence that the R6 base design broke old R4 instances.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No backwards-compatible base alternative is needed to preserve R4 instances because old data can simply omit these optional R6 elements. Standard extensions or profile-specific backports may be appropriate for R6-to-R4 exchange, but those are migration mitigations, not a less-breaking base R6 design.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: No R4-to-R6 base break; R6-to-R4 conversion may require extensions, sidecar storage, or lossy omission.

evidence.detail: R6 differential includes the listed optional fields.
No same-path native R4 elements were found.

examples.examplesMd: Base R4 cannot carry most of these fields without extensions or side-channel data.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 substantially enriches PaymentReconciliation. This is useful for new workflows but creates lossy reverse-version conversion for R4 consumers.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances remain valid with respect to these additions because all are optional. Valid R6 instances using them cannot be represented in base R4 without extensions or data loss.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Define a per-field R6→R4 policy: preserve in extensions, store externally, or drop with audit logging. R4→R6 systems may populate these fields from local payment records but are not required to.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Optional base additions are less disruptive than mandatory fields, but standard cross-version extensions would reduce reverse-conversion loss.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Allocation-specific additions overlap with the allocation findings but are grouped here for conversion planning.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: Canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, derivation, baseDefinition, and abstract flag are unchanged. Metadata status changed from draft to active and is noted separately.
No local minimum-cardinality increases were found beyond new mandatory root `type` and required renamed `date`; `amount` was relaxed from required to optional and is captured as a finding.
Local type changes are captured. Unchanged elements such as `created`, `period`, `request`, `requestor`, `paymentIdentifier`, and `formCode` keep their type declarations.

Reference target changes are captured for `paymentIssuer` and allocation request/response mappings. `request` remains `Reference(Task)` and `requestor` remains Practitioner/PractitionerRole/Organization.
`status` and `processNote.type` retain the same inspected local code sets. `outcome` and payment-type binding changes are findings. Full external expansions were not available.
No new local PaymentReconciliation-specific invariants were identified. Inherited `dom-*`, `ele-1`, and extension constraint differences are out of scope.
No local business element newly became a modifier or stopped being one. `status` remains a modifier; base `implicitRules` and `modifierExtension` are inherited and out of scope.
No local fixed value, pattern value, or default value changes were found.
